finding: At equal derivative order the Engine is more than 3× slower than FeOs, which would justify compiled low-order forward mode

Side note on Clapeyron: Engine/Clapeyron 1.5×–3.3× outside A=A (ties inside A=A: propane-liquid 1.6×, ethane-10000 1.6×), at least 3× only on the associating states O-P01/methanol-hexane, O-P01/methanol-liquid, O-P01/methanol-vapor. Pure neutral reduced Helmholtz energy, Engine/Clapeyron median ratio by order: value 2.4×, gradient 0.92× (ties inside A=A: propane-dilute 0.92×, propane-liquid 0.85×, ethane-100 0.92×, ethane-10000 0.95×, ethane-loop 0.94×), Hessian 1.4× (ties inside A=A: ethane-100 1.3×, ethane-loop 1.4×).

finding: Changed-control cost of the ASL equilibrium record
answer: The ASL equilibrium node averages 5.6× the native direct solve (7.74 ms vs 1.38 ms per node), but that average spans two nodes: 387 µs at the record's starting point (cached result) and 15 ms at changed controls. Native solves take about 1.38 ms per node, so the changed node costs about 11×, with identical values and derivatives. The cause is the path: the callback walks from its starting point to every other control by continuation each time (asl_adapter.cpp:466-483), while the native arm solves directly from fixed guesses. Indicative only on a loaded host.
evidence: statistics.csv T10 equilibrium/*; raw/T10.jsonl.gz per_row_seconds; asl_adapter.cpp:466-483
decision: Worth a design before the record is used inside process optimizers; any change must keep branch safety.
